q: 1. Into how many units are all the rocks geologically classified?
explain: Geologically, rocks are classified into three categories: Igneous, Sedimentary, and Metamorphic.

q: 2. The sedimentary rocks are formed due to ............
options: solidification of molten mass lying below or above the earth surface
gradual deposition of materials like sand, clay, etc., generally by setting water
alteration of original structure under heat and excessive pressure
explain: Sedimentary rocks (also called aqueous rocks) are formed by the accumulation and lithification of mineral or organic particles deposited over time, often in water bodies.

q: 3. Spalling hammer is used for ............
explain: A spalling hammer is a heavy hammer used in the initial stage of stone dressing to knock off large, irregular chunks (spalls) from a quarry stone.

q: 4. Good quality stones must ............
explain: A good building stone should be durable against weathering, free from internal flaws like clay pockets, and resistant to atmospheric acids in industrial areas.

q: 5. Granite mainly composed of quartz and feldspar particles, is obtained from ............
explain: Granite is a plutonic igneous rock formed by the slow cooling of magma deep beneath the earth's surface.

q: 6. Which of the following stone is best suited for construction of piers and abutments of a railway bridge?
explain: Granite is preferred for heavy engineering works like bridge piers because it possesses high crushing strength and durability.

q: 7. A rock contains only mineral. It is called ............
explain: Monomineralic rocks are composed essentially of a single mineral species (e.g., Dunite is mostly olivine).

q: 8. For a good building stone, its specific gravity should the greater than
explain: A high specific gravity (above 2.7) indicates a dense, compact stone with low porosity, which translates to better strength and durability for construction.

q: 9. Gneiss is obtained from
explain: Gneiss is a metamorphic rock formed by the high-grade regional metamorphism of pre-existing igneous rocks (like granite) or sedimentary rocks.

q: 10. The ultimate tensile strength of structural mild steel is about
explain: Structural mild steel typically has an ultimate tensile strength ranging between 420 and $540	ext{ N/mm}^2$.

q: 11. The crushing strength of a stone depends upon its ...............
explain: The strength of a stone is primarily determined by its grain structure (texture) and its density (indicated by specific gravity).

q: 12. The type of glass used for the window of bath room and toilets is ...............
explain: Ground glass is translucent; it allows light to pass through but scatters it so that objects cannot be seen clearly, providing privacy.

q: 13. Apiece of timber whose thickness and width are respectively 5 cm and 10 cm is called ...............
explain: Small pieces of timber used for specific framing or roofing tasks are often classified as strips when they meet these small dimensions.

q: 14. The minimum compressive strength of 1st class bricks should be ...............
explain: According to standard specifications, a First Class brick must have a minimum crushing or compressive strength of 105 kg/cm² (often rounded to 100 kg/cm² in many textbooks).

q: 15. The minimum compressive strength of 2nd class bricks should be ...............
explain: Second Class bricks are slightly less dense and durable than first class, with a minimum required compressive strength of 75 kg/cm².

q: 16. Slate in the form of tiles is used ...............
options: as an excellent roof covering material
explain: Slate is easily split into thin, impermeable sheets, making it one of the most durable and effective natural roofing materials.

q: 17. Sandstone consists of ...............
explain: a sedimentary rock that consists primarily of quartz and a cementing material, often silica (siliceous) or lime (calcareous).

q: 18. A good quality stone absorbs water less than ...............
explain: For high durability, a building stone should not absorb more than 5% of its dry weight in water after 24 hours of immersion.

q: 19. A stone is rejected if it absorbs water more than ...............
explain: If a stone absorbs more than 10% water, it is generally considered too porous and weak for structural use in permanent buildings.

q: 20. The silicious sandstone which has been subjected to metamorphic action, is called
explain: Quartzite is a hard, metamorphic rock which was originally pure quartz sandstone.

q: 21. The colour of statuary marble used for sculptor's work is ...............
explain: Statuary marble is famous for its pure white color and fine grain, which allows for detailed carving in statues.

q: 22. On Mohs' scale, a scratch with the aid of a finger nail indicates a hardness of .........
explain: The Mohs scale of mineral hardness characterizes the scratch resistance of various minerals. A fingernail has a hardness of about 2.5, so if a mineral can be scratched by a fingernail, its hardness is approximately 2 or less.

q: 23. Which of the following can be used as a preservative for building stones?
explain: Preservatives like linseed oil, coal tar, and alum soap solution are applied to stone surfaces to prevent the penetration of moisture and atmospheric gases, thereby increasing durability.

q: 24. Pointing is the process whereby .............
options: the masonry joints are filled up with mortar after raking out for small depth
the grooves are cut on a plastered surface to give a look of masonry
small circles looking like points are cut out at random on a plastered surface
explain: Pointing involves raking out the mortar joints to a depth of about 15-20mm and refilling them with a richer mortar to protect the joints and improve appearance.

q: 25. Mild steel is used for .............
options: structural works in beams, joints and girders
explain: Mild steel is ductile and strong in both tension and compression, making it perfect for structural members like beams and girders.

q: 26. Minimum of 40% of iron, is available in ............
explain: As Per Key B is the answer .

q: 27. The property of material enabling it to be drawn into thin wires is called ............
explain: Ductility is the mechanical property that allows a material (like mild steel) to deform under tensile stress and be drawn into wires.

q: 28. The radial splits which are wider on the outside of the log and narrower towards the pith are known as ............
explain: Star shakes are radial cracks that originate from the bark and extend towards the sapwood, often caused by extreme heat or frost.

q: 29. Plywood has the advantage of ............
options: greater tensile strength in longer direction
greater tensile strength in shorter direction
same tensile strength in all directions
explain: By gluing veneers with grains at right angles to each other, plywood achieves uniform strength properties in all longitudinal and transverse directions.

q: 30. The coefficient of linear expansion of granite is in the range of ............
explain: Granite has a low coefficient of thermal expansion, which is relatively comparable to that of glass.

q: 31. The fracture of a stone may be ............
explain: Depending on the mineral composition, a stone can break in even, uneven, or curved (conchoidal) patterns.

q: 32. Pick up the hypabyssal rock from the following ............
explain: Dolerite is the correct answer as it is the shallow-depth intrusive rock among the choices.

q: 33. Pick up the volcanic rock from the following ............
explain: Basalt is formed from the rapid cooling of lava on the surface, making it a volcanic igneous rock.

q: 34. In arches stratified stones are placed so that their planes are ............
explain: To resist the compressive forces in an arch effectively, the natural bedding planes of the stones should be radial (perpendicular to the line of thrust).
Basalt is a volcanic (extrusive) igneous rock formed by the rapid cooling of magnesium-rich and iron-rich lava at the surface.

q: 36. Seasoning of timber is done for ............
explain: Seasoning is the process of reducing the moisture content (sap) of timber to improve its stability, strength, and durability.
